text:
Recent evidence favors testing sampling and objective changes separately. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compares uniform, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive negatives: outcomes depend on dataset popularity skew; uniform sampling favors head items, while popularity-based sampling can improve balance at an accuracy cost. [Scalable Cross-Entropy, RecSys 2024](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26), approximates softmax using GPU-efficient selection of informative, high-scoring catalog items. These motivate affordable candidate-pool mining, but do not establish gains for masked BERT4Rec.

[Correcting the LogQ Correction, RecSys 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331), identifies a subtle error: negatives are sampled, but the positive is inserted deterministically. Its revised gradient correction treats these contributions separately and introduces an uncertainty-based sample weight. For a uniform/popularity mixture, correction must reflect the actual proposal distribution; after adaptive hard selection, using the original pool’s probabilities is not automatically valid. Sampling correction addresses distributional bias, not whether an unobserved item is actually relevant.

False-negative handling remains a separate problem. Earlier [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) explicitly models potential positives among negatives, although its teacher-based design is unsuitable for direct adoption under this task’s constraints. A conservative experimental inference: retain one BERT4Rec per category, exclude known training positives from negatives, mix random candidates with moderately hard candidates, and cap hardness rather than always selecting top scores. Compare this against corrected sampled softmax without mining; preserve masked-target training and appended-mask inference. Treat high scores as uncertain relevance, never verified negative labels. Select by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; stronger training margins alone are insufficient.
